headline: Indian Stock Market Crashes: Sensex Slumps 1,100 Points as US Bond Yields Hit 2002 Highs and Brent Nears $100

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: 10-year US Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2002, impacting global equity sentiment
Massive sell-off by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) who are selling Indian stocks en-masse
Rebound in crude oil prices with Brent crude nearing the $100 per barrel mark
Concerns over global rate hikes sparking significant capital outflows from emerging markets
whatHappening: Sensex crashed by 1,100 points while Nifty 50 dropped below the 22,300 mark during intraday trading
Over ₹10 trillion in investor wealth was wiped out in a single trading session as markets tumbled
Indian benchmarks are set for their longest weekly losing run in 25 years following consistent selling
Midcap and smallcap indices faced a sharp pullback, with several stocks hitting daily lows in the broader market
summary: Indian equity markets suffered a massive crash today, with the Sensex plunging 1,100 points and Nifty slipping below 22,300. The sell-off was driven by multi-decade high US bond yields, rising Brent crude prices nearing $100, and aggressive FII selling. Approximately ₹10 trillion of investor wealth was erased as broader markets also faced significant downward pressure.
